resolution: The persistent dark lines on the painted receiver were neither paint nor geometry gaps but flat-shading creases: editMeshToGeometry assigned every vertex its own face's Newell normal, so a curved low-poly part (the receiver: 284 faces, ~54 distinct normals confirmed from the mesh dump) showed a per-facet lighting seam at each edge — bilinear had smeared paint over them, and the nearest-sampler fix (req_1321) exposed them. Reworked editMeshToGeometry to emit SMOOTH vertex normals with a crease angle (SMOOTH_CREASE_DEG=40): each vertex averages only the adjacent faces within the crease angle of the current face, so gentle curve facets shade smoothly (seams vanish) while box corners stay hard. Hot-reloadable cart .ts; editMesh 92/92, cart bundles clean.
